# TornadoCash Demixer

> Open-source Python toolkit (MIT) for Tornado Cash forensics on public on-chain data. Given a depositor wallet it lists likely withdrawal addresses with an evidence band and the evidence behind each; it also groups exits paid out together, links wallets of one operator, follows withdrawn funds forward, and can run a placebo check that shows how many leads chance alone produces for the wallet. 56 verified pools on 8 EVM chains (Ethereum, BSC, Polygon, Arbitrum, Optimism, Avalanche, Gnosis, Base). Leads, not proof.

What the evidence supports, measured on real depositors with a placebo (target-decoy) test: a linked address (a direct counterparty of the depositor whose first withdrawal came within 72 h of the deposit, a withdrawal sent by the depositor's side, or an exchange deposit address both sent funds to, when it sweeps to a labelled exchange) and an early multi-pool profile match (10+ notes over 2+ pools, all received within 72 h) stand clearly above chance; a direct link withdrawn later than 72 h is chance-level, so since 2.17 it is shown as context only; amount+timing (count match, self-relay) and gas-price matches do not, so they never make a lead on their own. Gas price counts only on withdrawals the user sent (a relayer chooses the gas price of relayed ones). Bands: `strong` = lead signals from two independent sources (direct link, shared deposit address, early profile); `moderate` = a lead signal from one source; `weak` = amount+timing and/or gas price only, which never raise the band. The discrimination gate shrinks the field of count matches but does not separate real from chance ones. The shared-deposit signal needs an attribution set (exchange labels); without it, deposit addresses are shown as context only (`tornado-demix labels fetch` downloads the public set on request; it is not bundled).

Install: `python -m pip install tornado-demix` (CLI, from PyPI); the local Flask UI and the evaluation tools need a checkout (`python -m pip install ".[web]"`). Needs an Etherscan-family API key (config/api.csv or the ETHERSCAN_API_KEY environment variable).

## Commands

- `python -m tornado_demix demix <wallet>`: exit candidates for one depositor. Options: `--network`, `--window-days`, `--exit-window HOURS`, `--known-exit ADDR`, `--placebo`, `--no-deposit-addresses`, `--report file.html`, `--json file.json`.
- `python -m tornado_demix multi <wallet> <wallet> ...`: correlate several depositors (shared candidates, consolidators, shared funders, operator clusters).
- `python -m tornado_demix cluster <wallet>`: follow split exits one hop to a common collection address.
- `python -m tornado_demix characterize <address>`: an exit address and its main next hops, labelled when an attribution set is configured.
- `python -m tornado_demix trace <address> --amount N`: multi-hop FIFO trace of withdrawn funds with DEX-swap resolution.
- `python webui/app.py`: local web UI (http://127.0.0.1:5000) over the same functions.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/prettydeath/TornadoCash-demixer/blob/main/README.md): features, installation, configuration, documented public cases (Ronin, Wintermute, Beanstalk, KuCoin, Harmony), limitations
- [Methodology](https://github.com/prettydeath/TornadoCash-demixer/blob/main/docs/METHODOLOGY.md): signals, evidence families, bands, score, exit groups, operator graph, tracing
- [Evaluation](https://github.com/prettydeath/TornadoCash-demixer/blob/main/docs/EVALUATION.md): synthetic benchmark, placebo test on 152 real depositors, public cases, ENS-labelled set and the Wang et al. (2023) protocol

## Limits

- A careful user (relayers, delays, fresh split exits) leaves no linked address; the tool then reports no lead or only `weak` candidates.
- Bridges, other mixers and cross-chain hops are not followed.
- FIFO is used only to attribute withdrawn funds to later transfers when tracing forward; the tool does not match deposits to withdrawals by FIFO order (the temporal heuristic of Cristodaro et al., arXiv 2510.09433, a paper since withdrawn).
- Results depend on the explorer API and its rate limits.
